statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low on an orderly, narrow overnight tape; Stress stays elevated on three-year-high yields, oil above $90 and a stacked Sep 3-4 data calendar.
recommendation: Conditions are described as range-like through the Asian and European hours. Conditional risk is concentrated in the 13:30-16:00 UTC window covering the US cash open, the semiconductor reaction to Broadcom's guidance and the 14:00 UTC ISM Services PMI, where the mapped policy state is projected to move to WATCH.
headline: Post-Broadcom dip fully retraced overnight, keeping Tail low while yields near three-year highs hold Stress elevated
body: Nasdaq-100 futures are trading near 29,208 (+0.07%) inside an overnight band of roughly 80 points, 29,133 to 29,213. The low was printed after Broadcom's fiscal Q3 release, which beat on revenue at $29.6bn with AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7bn, up 221% year over year, but guided fourth-quarter revenue to about $34.8bn against consensus near $35.0bn; the shares fell in extended trading. That dip has been fully retraced in index futures, which is observed evidence that mean reversion is functioning rather than failing. The Sep 2 cash session closed at 29,143.33 (+0.23%, day range 28,971.90-29,165.62) and VIX finished at 15.20 after a near 7% decline. Asia is mixed on Sep 3, with the Kospi up about 0.9%, the Topix up about 0.7%, the Nikkei little changed near 64,456 in the middle of its daily range, and the ASX 200 marginally higher. No persistent one-way structure, shallow-pullback sequence or session-extreme holding is observed, so Tail stays low. Stress remains elevated: the US 10-year is near 4.777% after reaching an intraday 4.814% on Sep 2, its highest since November 2023, the 30-year is above 5.2%, WTI is near $91 and Brent near $95.60 with the Strait of Hormuz still largely closed to normal commercial transit. Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks have left roughly 60% odds on a September 16 hike, and New York Fed President Williams framed the yield surge as a reflection of economic strength rather than dysfunction. The scheduled path into the next 24 hours runs through the 12:30 UTC claims and trade block, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC ISM Services PMI, with August payrolls falling outside this window on Sep 4.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the assessment de-escalated and then stabilised. The Asian and European hours of Sep 2 carried Tail in the 20-23 band under an event/whipsaw then trend-down reading as the global long-end selloff pressed on index futures. From the 12:00 UTC hour Tail fell below the WATCH threshold to EA_ON as yields paused, Williams' remarks steadied sentiment and the cash session recovered, reaching a low of 11 in the late US evening. Broadcom's after-close guidance produced a futures dip that was retraced within the overnight band rather than extending, and the published readings settled near Tail 12 with Stress near 55. Five hourly slots have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are projected to stay range-like through the remaining Asian and European sessions, with a modest step up around the European cash open as the regional semiconductor complex prices Broadcom's fourth-quarter guidance. Conditional risk concentrates in the 12:30-16:00 UTC block covering jobless claims and the trade balance, the US cash open and the ISM Services PMI. The mapped policy state is projected to move to WATCH for the 14:00 and 15:00 UTC hours on peak conditional Tail of 21, then decay back to EA_ON through the US afternoon. A modest late uptick is projected into the 19:00 UTC power hour on closing-auction flow and pre-payrolls positioning, after which conditions are projected to normalise into a compressed overnight band ahead of the Sep 4 payrolls report, which falls outside this window.
